proposal.claim:
ORIGIN, STATED FIRST. This is NOT from reports/SCOUT.jsonl, and the reason is the evaluator rather than the notebook. Eighteen payers are in it now. Twelve are anchored to a wall-clock instant or an announcement -- the quarterly 07:00-08:00 UTC delivery fixing on the last Friday of a quarter, the Deribit expiry and Dual Investment 07:30-08:00 windows, the CME 15:00-16:00 London hour, the Monday 00:00 UTC liquidity-provider tier reset, the daily 00:00 UTC tournament qualification reset, the pre-announced margin-tier change, the jurisdiction offboarding deadlines, the BUSD collateral wind-down, the delisting settlement -- and no field of TrialConfig or SignalTrialConfig names a date, an hour or a weekday. A Track A programme is anchored only to its own start offset, the runner enumerates offsets on a fixed stride and reports a percentile taken across all of them, so any weekday or hour-of-day phase is averaged away by construction rather than measured; there is no field that selects offsets by calendar position. Five more -- forced short covering, short-gamma delta hedging, leveraged-token rebalancing, copy-trade replication, TWAP child orders -- need either an intrabar forced-flow proxy or a rule that trades WITH the move. H0008 and H0009 died discovering the first is absent, and H0013 died discovering the second is too: orc/eval/simulate.py gate_below_sma is out[ok] = close[ok] <= sma[ok], so sma:<days> is a weakness-buying gate of the same sign as dip:, not a trend gate. The venue-outage line is right that its observable is the only one reachable entirely from the held panel, but "bars missing simultaneously across the cross-section" is data forensics rather than a rule any config field expresses, and its honest home is a scout or robustness pass at zero ledger rows. This reading is not being re-derived to fill space: H0011, H0012 and H0013 all made it and no adversary disputed it.

WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THAT, because it is the durable finding of this pass and belongs in a registered claim rather than in a conversation. Track B cannot be extended at all right now: SignalTrialConfig.rule accepts only carry_funding and carry_funding_long, and both belong to families already closed (H0002, H0006). On Track A, every gate the vocabulary offers buys weakness and that family is closed (H0007); leverage above 1x is closed (KT-2) and its sweep was refused again as H0012; stride_days, n_contributions, hold_days and include_funding are H0001's own axes and were refused as a finer grid (H0011); the cost axes are what scripts/robustness.py stresses over recorded cells at zero ledger rows, and clock is what scripts/execution_realism.py re-runs at zero ledger rows. That leaves exactly two fields of the entire vocabulary with no row behind them, and the repository says so itself rather than my asserting it: orc/orchestrator/runner.py records, in the comment on the fix described below, "of 1332 Track A rows, none has take_profit or stop_loss set". This hypothesis is the whole of that remaining surface, asked once, in one grid.

WHO IS STRUCTURALLY PAYING, AND WHY THEY KEEP DOING IT. The accumulating long on a perpetual, and the constraint is the instrument rather than a preference. A perpetual has no expiry and no delivery, so there is no date on which the position converts into the asset and the funding obligation ends. The only way to stop paying is to close, and a programme defined as a schedule of deposits held to horizon by construction never closes. KT-1 already measured this bill from the paying side -- a median 36% of contributed capital over a three-year weekly DCA, with 87% of BTC settlements positive -- and that figure is an integral over notional and time, not a constant: funding is charged on the mark notional every eight hours, so the holder who is right pays more per hour precisely because they are right, and a programme that keeps depositing raises the notional the charge is levied on with every deposit. The payment ends the day the accumulator can hold the spot asset instead, which inside this venue's USDs-M book they cannot; that is what makes it structural and recurring rather than a bad week.

WHY THIS PAYER IS NOT ONE ALREADY TESTED. H0002 and H0006 stood on the funding rate's sign and level and asked whether a timing rule could collect it from someone else. H0007 and H0009 stood on the liquidated leveraged long and asked whether a gate could buy their forced selling. H0001 names no payer at all and exists as the control. Here nothing is collected from anyone and nothing is detected: the payment is continuous, unconditional, and ours, and the only question is whether ending it early is worth the upside forgone. That is a different logical structure from the one codex rejected in H0008 -- "a generic aggregate take-profit fires on any price rise ... a generic terminating take-profit hypothesis with a forced-cover mechanism attached only in prose" -- because there is no flow here to identify. A cost that is always on does not need a detector, and the objection that a threshold cannot separate forced buying from ordinary trend does not reach a rule that is not trying to.

WHAT IS NEW SINCE H0008 DIED, since repeating a rejection already on the record spends a pass for nothing. H0008 was killed on 2026-09-03 because run_dca_trial priced early-exiting paths with the registered n_contributions and the nominal horizon, so a programme that took profit in week 5 was charged for 151 deposits it never made and an ensemble whose true annualised IRR was +415% was recorded at the bracket floor -0.9999. That defect is closed in the working tree: the path-dependent branch now derives the deposits that actually landed as invested / contribution and uses out["exit_bar"] as elapsed time, and its comment names H0008 as the family it was closed before. Every metric this kill condition reads is therefore priced on the path that actually happened. Nothing else of H0008 is reused -- its mechanism, its include_funding axis, its take_profit levels and its universe are all replaced -- and in particular there is no include_funding axis here, because claude's objection to H0011 was exactly that funding_frac_q50 is recorded on every funded row for free; clause 3 below spends no cells on it and reads the recorded quantity instead.

THE RULE SHAPE. A DCA that can end on its own profit-and-loss state. Fifteen cells: take_profit in {null, 0.15, 0.35, 0.75, 1.50} crossed with stop_loss in {null, 0.20, 0.40}, both evaluated by the simulator as pnl divided by contributed capital, on a fixed weekly schedule of 156 deposits -- 1092 days, KT-1's own three-year frame, so funding_frac_q50 here is directly comparable with the 36% KT-1 measured. Every Track A row in the ledger runs to horizon; a programme carrying an exit rule is a different object, not a different setting of an existing one, and the zero-row count above is the evidence for that rather than my assertion of it. The (null, null) cell is the control and is deliberately H0001's funded (156, 7) cell re-run inside this run under one code hash, so the comparison is made within a run rather than across two.

THE UNIVERSE AND WHY THESE SIX. Six symbols keeps the enumeration at 90 configurations, inside MAX_PROBE_CONFIGURATIONS = 96 for a mechanism with no rows. Three of them are above zero on H0001's published baseline (BTCUSDT +0.362, ETHUSDT +0.679, SOLUSDT +0.373) and three below it (XRPUSDT -0.053, DOGEUSDT -0.099, ADAUSDT -0.320), so the family cannot be read on a set of symbols that only rose. That split is a property of the control and is already printed in reports/CYCLE_REPORT.md; it is not a selection on anything about take_profit or stop_loss, which have no rows to select on. All six are known to admit the (156, 7) schedule, since CYCLE_REPORT.md reports that cell for each of them.

WHAT THIS IS A PARTIAL TEST OF, AND WHAT IT CANNOT REACH. Two things, said plainly. First, stop_loss here is a threshold on pnl over contributed capital, which is not the margin ratio the venue's liquidation engine actually watches; it is a proxy for leaving before that engine fires, and clause 2 measures the proxy against the recorded liquidation_rate rather than assuming it works. Codex's objection to H0010 -- that a margin rule constrains equity or peak-to-trough loss and not pnl over cumulative contributions -- is correct, and is the reason stop_loss is a secondary axis under test here and not the mechanism being claimed. Second, terminating on a profit-and-loss state is not the same as terminating on the funding bill, which no field of TrialConfig expresses; a take_profit fires on a price rise whatever caused it. Clause 3 is what forces the mechanism named above to be the thing measured rather than a price-path artefact, by requiring the improvement to be ordered across symbols by the bill the control actually paid.

ONE PRE-EMPTION. That an adversary can run these 90 cells in under a minute at zero ledger rows is true of every hypothesis this project will ever propose and is not by itself an argument against registering one; it was decisive against H0012 because the answer there was already implied by KT-2 and by a monotonicity anyone could state in advance. Nothing in the ledger implies the answer here. No row carries take_profit or stop_loss, so whether truncation helps or hurts the left tail is unmeasured, and clause 3's cross-symbol ordering against the recorded funding bill is not implied by any recorded result.
proposal.kill_condition:
NOTATION. Every cell is contribution 100, stride_days 7, n_contributions 156, hold_days 0, leverage 1.0, gate none, include_funding true, clock 1h. For symbol s, C(s) is the (take_profit null, stop_loss null) control cell. A(s, c) is the recorded mwrr_q05 of cell c, the annualised money-weighted return at the 5th percentile of start dates. L(s, c) is the recorded liquidation_rate and F(s, c) the recorded funding_frac_q50. G(s) = max over the fourteen non-control cells of [A(s, c) - A(s, C(s))], and c*(s) is a cell attaining that maximum. The universe is six symbols. Every threshold below is frozen now, before any of these cells has been run.

WHY mwrr_q05 AND NOT tm_q05. take_profit and stop_loss end different cells at different times, so the cells of this grid do not hold for the same length of time. CLAUDE.md section 4 says tm_q05 may not be compared between cells that hold for different lengths, and that the annualised IRR is the comparison which survives a horizon change. tm_q05 is reported for every cell and is not argued from in any clause below.

1. THE EXIT DOES NOTHING AT THE LEFT TAIL. Closed if G(s) <= 0 on four or more of the six symbols. A programme that can end and still fails to beat running to horizon at the 5th percentile of start dates, on a majority of the universe, has no case: the upside it gave up cost more than the obligation it stopped.

2. IT DOES NOT TOUCH RUIN. Consider only the symbols with L(s, C(s)) >= 0.10, i.e. those where the funded control is actually being liquidated. Closed also -- even if clause 1 is cleared -- if fewer than half of those symbols satisfy L(s, c*(s)) <= 0.5 * L(s, C(s)). If no symbol has L(s, C(s)) >= 0.10, this clause is inapplicable and must be reported as inapplicable rather than as passed. The claim is that an exit rule takes the programme out of the venue's liquidation engine before it fires; if the best-improving cell is liquidated on nearly as many start dates as the control, then whatever the gain in clause 1 is, it is not that.

3. THE GAIN IS NOT THE FUNDING BILL. Order the six symbols by F(s, C(s)), the funding the control actually paid as a fraction of contributed capital. Let Hi be the median of G(s) over the three symbols with the largest F, and Lo the median of G(s) over the three with the smallest. Closed also if Hi <= Lo. If ending the obligation early is what pays, the symbols that were paying most must gain most; if the improvement is unordered with respect to the recorded bill, the exit is a price-path artefact and the mechanism named in the claim is not the thing that was measured. This clause is the discriminator and no single symbol can satisfy it. It is deliberately asymmetric: with six symbols split three and three it is a weak test in the direction of survival and a meaningful one in the direction of closure, so surviving it must be reported as "not falsified" and never as confirmation.

4. IT IS A FITTED THRESHOLD, NOT A RULE. Closed also if the project's own shape diagnostic reports SPIKE at the best cell on four or more of the six symbols. take_profit carries four numeric levels and stop_loss two, so every interior take_profit level has a neighbour on each side and the diagnostic has something to read. A termination threshold that works at one setting and not one step away is a corner of the grid, which CLAUDE.md section 6 says is not a finding no matter how large its value.

Closing requires any one clause to fire. Survival requires all four to fail, and survival does not make this shape a result: it earns a second registration under a new id, as section 6 provides for a mechanism that has survived its own kill condition.

verdict.reason: [claude] 제안된 90셀을 원장 0행으로 그대로 돌려보니 판정 통계 mwrr_q05가 메커니즘이 아니라 청산 속도를 재고 있다: stop_loss가 걸린 모든 셀은 tm_q05가 0.44~0.78인데도(ETHUSDT (None,0.20): tm_q05 0.669) 브래킷 하한 -0.9999에 고정되어 통제군의 완전손실 -1.0과 구분되지 않고, take_profit 셀은 수 주 만에 종료된 구간을 연환산해 SOLUSDT (1.5,None) +76.89, DOGEUSDT (1.5,None) +43.62를 기록하므로 G(s)는 '의무를 일찍 끝낸 값어치'가 아니라 '목표에 얼마나 빨리 닿았나'다. 그 결과 1·2·3절은 모두 발동 불가(G=+2.87/+6.60/+77.89/+7.43/+44.62/+6.71로 6/6 양수, L(c*)=0.000으로 2절 5/5 통과, Hi=+44.62 > Lo=+6.60)이고 4절만 SPIKE 5/6으로 발동하므로, 등록은 이미 확정된 CLOSED를 90행 값으로 사는 것이며 그 CLOSED조차 연환산 인공물이지 청구서 종료 메커니즘의 측정이 아니다. | [codex] The named payer is the strategy itself, and the proposed rule explicitly makes that payer stop paying by closing early; avoided self-incurred funding cost is not a structural counterparty that continues transferring value when the rule scales. The four clauses do provide concrete numerical closure conditions, but falsifiability cannot repair the missing structural payer.
